newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab Investment says 11-mth operating profit up.
newsitem.headline: Arab Investment says 11-mth operating profit up.

text.p: The Riyadh-based Arab Investment Company S.A.A. (TAIC) said on Saturday its operating profit in the first 11 months of 1996 had soared to $26 million from $17.5 million in the year-ago period.
A statement by the investment company, established in 1974 by 15 Arab countries, said it was discussing increasing its capital base to $400 million from $300 million.

The company said it was currently investing in 34 projects in the Arab world worth $220 million. It said the projects ranged from agriculture and industry to the services sector, but gave no further details.
TAIC, a joint stock company, owns an offshore banking unit with the same name in Bahrain and invests in Arab projects.
The shareholders are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Sudan, Egypt, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Syria, Iraq, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco, Libya, Oman and Yemen.
